# Alert Handler Register Wrapper — Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

This module provides the register and interrupt wrapper for the alert handler block. It implements the software-visible control/status register (CSR) interface, generates the four class interrupt outputs, provides the hardware-facing configuration and status mapping used by the alert handler logic, and produces a latchable crashdump snapshot.

The module is not itself the alert classification, escalation, or ping engine. It is the boundary between those hardware functions and the software-programmed register state.

## 2. Interface Overview

The module shall provide:

- A TileLink-UL device interface for CSR read and write transactions.
- Four interrupt outputs, one per alert class.
- A crashdump output carrying state information for hardware debug or recovery logic.
- A fatal integrity alert output.
- Hardware status/control sideband inputs and outputs for the alert handler logic.
- A normal reset and a dedicated shadowed-register reset.

## 3. Reset Behavior

- The normal reset shall:
  - Clear all non-shadowed registers.
  - Reset interrupt state so no class interrupt is asserted after reset.
  - Clear the crashdump latch and latched snapshot.
  - Re-arm the crashdump capture mechanism.

- The shadowed-register reset shall:
  - Reset all shadowed configuration registers.
  - Be used to place the shadowed register state into a known, consistent reset value.

## 4. CSR and Bus Access Behavior

The module shall implement the full alert handler register address map.

It shall:

- Accept TileLink-UL read and write transactions to defined addresses.
- Return valid read data for readable registers.
- Perform writes only to writable fields.
- Ignore writes to locked or write-protected registers.
- Enforce write-1-to-clear behavior on sticky status fields, such as interrupt state and cause bits.
- Enforce clear-enable protection: writes to clear registers must be ignored when the corresponding clear-enable register is cleared.
- Reflect shadowed-register semantics for all critical configuration fields.

## 5. Configuration Outputs to the Alert Handler

The module shall output the programmed configuration values to the alert handler logic. These include:

- Ping timer enable.
- Ping timeout cycle count.
- For each alert channel:
  - Alert enable.
  - Alert class assignment.
  - A ping-enable indication that is asserted only when the alert is both enabled and locked.
- For each local alert:
  - Local alert enable.
  - Local alert class assignment.
- For each class:
  - Class enable.
  - Autolock enable.
  - Escalation signal enable bits.
  - Escalation phase-to-signal mapping.
  - Accumulation threshold.
  - Interrupt timeout cycle count.
  - Escalation phase cycle counts.
  - Crashdump trigger phase configuration.
  - Class clear indication, asserted when software writes 1 to the class clear register while clearing is permitted.

A class shall be considered enabled only when both:

- The class master enable is set, and
- At least one escalation signal enable within that class is set.

## 6. Hardware Status Updates into the Register File

The module shall update register state from hardware status inputs as follows.

### 6.1 Alert Cause Bits

For each alert channel, when the hardware cause input is asserted, the corresponding cause bit shall be set in the register file.

The cause bit is sticky:

- Once set, it shall remain set until software clears it.
- Further assertions of the same cause shall not clear it.
- Software clearing shall use write-1-to-clear semantics.

The same behavior shall apply to local alert cause bits.

### 6.2 Class Status Registers

The module shall reflect the current hardware status of each class in the register file:

- Current accumulation count.
- Current escalation counter value.
- Current escalation state.

These fields shall be readable by software and shall track the values provided by the alert handler logic.

### 6.3 Class Clear Autolock

For each class, when all of the following conditions are true:

- The class is enabled.
- The class autolock configuration is enabled.
- The hardware indicates that an escalation trigger has occurred for that class,

then the module shall automatically clear the class clear-enable register to zero.

After this automatic lock takes effect, software writes to the class clear register shall be ignored, and the class escalation state cannot be cleared through the register interface.

## 7. Interrupt Generation

The module shall generate one interrupt output per alert class.

For each class:

- The interrupt state bit shall be set when a hardware class trigger event is asserted.
- The interrupt state bit shall also be set when software performs a self-test write to the corresponding interrupt test field.
- The interrupt output shall be asserted only when:
  - The interrupt state bit is set, and
  - The interrupt enable bit for that class is set.
- The interrupt state bit shall remain set until software clears it through the interrupt state register.
- Clearing the interrupt state bit shall deassert the interrupt output unless a new trigger event has set it again.

Interrupt self-test writes shall affect only interrupt state. They must not set alert cause bits or increment class accumulation counters.

## 8. Crashdump Output

The crashdump output shall contain:

- All alert cause bits.
- All local alert cause bits.
- Current class accumulation counts.
- Current class escalation counts.
- Current class escalation states.

Until a crashdump latch condition has occurred, the crashdump output shall reflect the current live values from the register file and hardware status inputs.

When the crashdump latch request is asserted and the latch has not already been captured, the module shall:

- Capture the current crashdump values into an internal snapshot.
- Assert the latched state.
- Hold the crashdump output at the captured snapshot values.

After the snapshot has been captured:

- The crashdump output shall remain constant at the latched values.
- Subsequent changes to live status values shall not affect the output.
- Subsequent assertions of the crashdump latch request shall be ignored.

The crashdump capture mechanism shall be re-armed only by reset.

## 9. Shadowed Register Error Reporting

The module shall monitor all shadowed configuration registers for two classes of errors:

- Storage errors: the shadow copy differs from the main register copy, indicating a storage integrity failure.
- Update errors: a write transaction did not update the main and shadow copies consistently.

The module shall combine the error indications from all shadowed registers into two aggregate outputs:

- One aggregate storage error output.
- One aggregate update error output.

Each aggregate output shall be asserted if any monitored shadowed register reports the corresponding error class, and shall be deasserted only when no monitored shadowed register reports that error class.

## 10. Fatal Integrity Alert

The module shall assert the fatal integrity alert output when the register file detects an internal integrity or bus integrity failure.

This output shall be treated as a fatal condition by the surrounding alert handling logic.

# Specification: Alert Handler Register Wrapper

## 1. Overview

This module provides the register-interface layer for the alert handler. It contains all software-accessible configuration, status, interrupt, and clear registers. It also generates the four alert-class interrupts, exposes programmed configuration to the alert-processing logic, collects hardware status for software visibility, provides a crashdump snapshot output, and reports aggregate shadowed-register errors.

The module does not itself perform alert classification, accumulation, escalation, or ping testing. Instead, it acts as the boundary between those hardware functions and the software-visible register file.

## 2. Functional Behavior

### 2.1 Reset Behavior

The module shall support a normal reset and a separate shadowed-register reset.

On reset:

- All configuration and status registers shall be initialized to their hardware reset values.
- All interrupt pending state shall be cleared, and all interrupt outputs shall be deasserted.
- The crashdump latch shall be cleared, so that the crashdump output returns to live state.
- All shadowed-register error indications shall be deasserted.

### 2.2 Bus Register Access

The module shall act as a device on the system bus and shall provide read and write access to all implemented registers.

The module must:

- Correctly decode incoming bus transactions and generate the appropriate bus response.
- Allow software to read all status and configuration registers.
- Allow software to write writable configuration, interrupt, clear, and test registers.
- Apply all register access semantics, including write-enable protection, write-1-to-clear behavior, shadowed-write behavior, and locked-register behavior.
- Assert a fatal integrity alert output when the register file detects a bus-integrity violation.

### 2.3 Interrupt Generation

The module shall generate one interrupt output for each of the four alert classes: class A, class B, class C, and class D.

For each class:

- The interrupt shall be asserted when the class interrupt is enabled and a class interrupt is pending.
- The pending state shall be set when the alert-processing logic indicates that an alert has been classified into that class.
- The pending state shall also be set when software writes the corresponding interrupt test bit.
- The pending state shall be cleared by software through the interrupt state register.
- The interrupt output shall remain asserted while the pending bit is set and the enable bit is set, and shall deassert when software clears the pending bit or disables the enable bit.

### 2.4 Alert Cause Registers

The module shall provide one sticky cause bit for each external alert source and one sticky cause bit for each local alert source.

For each cause bit:

- When the corresponding alert-cause hardware event is asserted, the cause bit shall be set and shall remain set until software clears it.
- Software clearing shall be performed through the cause register.
- If the triggering condition is still present at the time of clearing, the cause bit shall be set again by the still-active event.
- The state of all cause bits shall be visible to software and shall be included in the crashdump snapshot.

### 2.5 Hardware Status Registers

The module shall expose the current hardware status of the alert-processing logic to software.

For each alert class, the following status information shall be visible to software:

- The current alert accumulation count.
- The current escalation counter value.
- The current escalation protocol state.

These values are driven by hardware and shall not be directly writable by software, except that software may clear the accumulation counter and abort an escalation sequence through the class clear mechanism described below.

### 2.6 Configuration Outputs

The module shall expose all software-programmed configuration values to the alert-processing logic.

The module shall provide:

- The ping timer enable setting.
- The ping timeout cycle count.
- For each external alert source:
  - Whether the alert is enabled.
  - Which alert class it is assigned to.
  - Whether the alert is eligible for ping testing. An alert shall be ping-eligible only when it is both enabled and its configuration is locked.
- For each local alert source:
  - Whether the local alert is enabled.
  - Which alert class it is assigned to.
- For each class:
  - Whether the class is enabled. A class shall be considered enabled only if the class master enable is set and at least one of the four escalation signal enables is set.
  - Whether the class lock / autolock option is set.
  - The enable state of each of the four escalation signals.
  - The phase-to-escalation-signal mapping for each of the four escalation phases.
  - The escalation accumulation threshold.
  - The interrupt timeout cycle count.
  - The duration of each of the four escalation phases.
  - The crashdump trigger setting, indicating which escalation phase shall cause the crashdump to be latched.

### 2.7 Class Clear Behavior

The module shall support software clearing of the per-class accumulation counter and escalation state through a class clear register.

For each class:

- Software writing the appropriate clear value shall generate a clear command to the alert-processing logic.
- The clear operation shall be protected by a per-class clear-enable bit.
- If the clear-enable bit is deasserted, the clear command shall not be generated.

The clear-enable bit may be deasserted by software. In addition, the module shall automatically deassert the clear-enable bit for a class when all of the following conditions are true:

- The class is enabled.
- The class lock / autolock option is set.
- The alert-processing logic indicates that an escalation-trigger event has occurred for that class.

Once automatically deasserted, the clear-enable bit shall remain deasserted until reset.

### 2.8 Crashdump Output

The module shall provide a crashdump output that contains a hardware-readable snapshot of key alert-handler state.

The crashdump contents shall include:

- All external alert cause bits.
- All local alert cause bits.
- The current accumulation counter for each class.
- The current escalation counter for each class.
- The current escalation state for each class.

The crashdump output shall operate as follows:

- After reset, the output shall present the live, current state.
- When the crashdump latch trigger is asserted and no snapshot has been latched yet, the module shall capture the current crashdump contents and hold them on the output.
- After a snapshot has been latched, subsequent assertions of the latch trigger shall be ignored.
- The latched snapshot shall remain on the output until reset.
- After reset, the output shall return to live state and the latching mechanism shall be re-armed.

### 2.9 Shadowed-Register Error Aggregation

The module shall provide two aggregate error indications for its shadowed registers:

- A shadowed storage error indication, asserted when any shadowed register detects that its storage copies disagree.
- A shadowed update error indication, asserted when any shadowed register detects an invalid or inconsistent update attempt.

These indications shall assert whenever at least one shadowed register reports the corresponding error condition. They shall deassert when no shadowed register reports such a condition.

### 2.10 Fatal Integrity Alert

The module shall assert a fatal integrity alert output whenever the register file detects an integrity violation. This output is intended to indicate a hardware or bus-integrity failure and shall be deasserted when the register file is not reporting such a failure.

## 3. Requirements Summary

In summary, the module must:

- Provide the complete software-visible register interface for the alert handler.
- Generate four class interrupts that are controlled by enable, pending, and test registers.
- Maintain sticky cause bits for external and local alerts.
- Reflect hardware status in software-readable registers.
- Expose software configuration to the alert-processing logic.
- Enforce clear protection, including automatic protection after escalation when configured.
- Provide a latching crashdump output.
- Report fatal bus-integrity failures and aggregate shadowed-register errors.
